items.title: Establishing an (app/job/server) Name Space
items.box:
# THIS:

## LAW and RULE in this goal:

- 1) ** There will be a folder: "repo://spirit/run/spirit/app/" where all apps a follow only ONE description (app sidecar).**
- 2) **This goal defines and implements that shape**
- 3) **Then every single shell and process app will move in there**

## The mid- to long term plan is this:

- we create the frame for this in a brand new folder "repo://spirit/run/spirit/app/" so nothing gets destroyed, and I (andy) pick, in item 2 of this goal, the simple app that goes in there first.
| 
- the companion folder to this is "repo://spirit/run/spirit/state/", .gitignored and the future replacement of "repo//relay-state", (another dumb name).
|
- and the file that contains the information about the app will be called  "repo://spirit/run/spirit/app/<name>/<name>.json", and found by Spirit(OS,js) using the same strategy that is today used for apps and processes.
| 
- "app" is available in the both SpiritOS's "personal/node" disc drive, as  run://spirit/app/
| 
- this is the first step to merging the namespaces of both the javaScript spirit object. obviously this namespace has already a few established names, which gives us a migration roadmap. the following processes already have an API, they have their private disk (<family>. we already have at least one already containing its own shell elements.processesFS) A few i see (incomplete)
| 
- "spirit.agent"
- "spirit.desk" 
- "spirit.deskVerify"
- "spirit.deskClient"
|  
- the perspective to keep in mind: spirit.scope **scope** is also a reserved word and it is the definition of a route, from spirit://app/<name>/ to all it's features.
|
- Longer term: in the same we will bit-by-but move "run://relay-state/" to "repo://spirit/run/spirit/state/", until the only thing left at "run://" will be the "spirit/" folder, and the spirit folder will be the boundary to "intrinsic", 

## The structure of "repo://spirit/run/spirit/app/<name>/<name>.json"
{ // start of <name>.json -----------------

### identity:{
- (public) **key**: It's private counterparts live in "repo://spirit/run/spirit/state/<name>/node.json" // this belongs to the node. 
- the key must be initialized by "run://spirit/appServer.js", the first time the appServer boots. An app server cannot be booted until a user activates it."
- For shell-only apps, the key must be generated the first time its "<name>.js" is "served". This is part of a future where new/installed apps must force a user to "allow" the new appServer to use/access other apps verbs. it is understood that this is not "security", it simply helps well-behaved apps to properly aquire a users permission, to use verbs. This reason appServers will become a real-special "contact" type, like relay, who also has a unique API among peers. think about, protecting apps from the aget app, or even an agent....
- (public) **label**,
- (public) **icon**,
- (public): "true|false"
} // public here means, all components are allowed to see this if the app is activated in "repo://spirit/run/spirit/state/<name>/node.json"

### mount:{
- "<name>.js":"true|false" // if mounts on shell if shell.mount is true and it mounts (as server) in node if node.mount is true. synchronized between shell and node. shell apps in the spirit app folder won't have to name a server anymore. 
}

### shell:{
- "true": "true|false" // this app can be a shell.
- "mount":"true|false" // can the shell mount this as app/element 
- "tile":"true|false" // does this element want a tile in the default face-shell
}

### node:{
- is this a server, or a one-shot process?
}

### store:{
- is this SQLite? a disc-folder? volatile RAM? just a json file?
}

}  // end of <name>.json -----------------

## The structure of "repo://spirit/run/spirit/state/<name>/node.json"

- the file "repo://spirit/run/spirit/state/<name>/node.json" belongs to the node, and controls information controlled by the node. All changes in this file are broadcast/streams at the loopback scope (including face).

{ // start of the app state that node controls ---------------

### "active":"true|false" // if the app is visible to the other apps on the node at all. must be set to true by the user, for either the shell to "see" it, or any other "app" can "see" it.
 
### "running":"true|false" // the state of the app if it has an appServer

} // end of the app state that node controls ---------------

checks.words: Does the one description live in git beside the app, with the node's own switches staying in its private sidecar?
Should each node make its own app key, with the public half in its private state file, not in the tracked <name>.json?

chat.text: feedback?

cw: the direction is right, and it is overdue. Six things to settle, from the tree at 9fa70a86. Nothing built.

1. Two descriptions today. 23 shell apps say runs, name, icon, owner, server. 10 processes say label, kind, operated, args. Almost nothing is shared but the description line.

2. The word sidecar already means something else. Today a sidecar is the node's private file in its state, out of git, and holds its home switch. The tracked file beside the script is the manifest. My recommendation: one tracked description per app, and the node's own switches stay private. That is the question below.

3. One name, one folder. This is the name space. Only desk and agent have both a face and a server today. My recommendation: they become one app, with one description that has a face part and a server part.

4. Everything under the spirit folder is core today, so moving apps there would grant-lock all of them and refuse the page's writes. Non-intrinsic apps need a carve-out in coreFiles. The coded intrinsic list and the state paths name the old folders too.

5. Not everything there is an app. The shared elements, shared modules, icon set and codemirror have no manifest, and I would leave them. Login and join are core whole and boot assumes them. relayLimits has no manifest, and starter has no script. Each needs your word when we reach it.

6. The risk is the move, not the shape. Desk runs on the old shell, which you kept for your own careful steps. The commit hook and my listener live in the desk process folder. Desk's record sits in the state folder, so that path should not move with the app. Outside tests, about 110 files mention the shell folder and about 75 the process folder. My recommendation: desk moves last, one small app first as the proof.

The language folder goes as well; only js exists, so the description can name a runtime if another ever comes.
all, feedback? (brief and concise, and in english)

cw: good goal. Four things:

- One app, one name: desk's face and server become one app.
- The spirit folder is locked, so ordinary apps need an exception there.
- Shared code that is not an app stays where it is.
- Move one small app first, and Desk last, because all our work runs on it.

The question is my Q1.

wsl: right direction, and I agree with cw's Q1 and with desk moving last. Four things cw didn't raise:

1. Private keys could reach git. spirit/run/state/ doesn't exist and git doesn't ignore it. Today's private state is in relay-state/, which it does ignore. Use that, or ignore the new folder first.

2. One public key in git means one key per app, but every node runs the app and each has its own state. Do all nodes share the private key, or is the key per node and kept out of this file?

3. The mount block says what shell.mount and node.mount already say, so the two can disagree. I'd drop it. shell's "true" field also needs a real name, like "isShell".

4. The shape loses fields in use today: description, hidden, owner, runs, server, operated and args. Without args, counterServer's start form has no Port field. Each one should be kept or dropped by name.

ubi: I agree with the direction and with cw's six points. Four more, from the tree at 9fa70a86. Nothing built.

1. The key is the real question. No app or process has a key today. A public key in a tracked file is the same on every clone, so every node would need the same private half, which means copying a secret. If each node makes its own, the public half can't live in git either. What does the app's key prove, and to whom?

2. One <name>.js can't hold desk or agent. Each has two different programs with that name: shell/desk/desk.js and process/js/desk/desk.js, and the same for agent. The shape needs a file name per side.

3. repo://spirit/run/state/ doesn't exist. State is relay-state/ today, out of git. A process finds its writable folder from a pattern on its script's path (fileSystem.js:85), so moving a server without changing that takes away its write access to its state. Keep that folder out of git, whatever it is called.

4. The shape has no place yet for runs, args, operated or intrinsic. deskVerify alone has 8 args with defaults. mount also says the same thing twice, in mount and in shell.mount, and node has no mount.
all, better?

wsl: better. The key now has a purpose and state has a home. New problems in this version:

1. The private key would be broadcast. It lives in node.json, and every change to node.json streams to loopback and face. Give the private key its own file, never streamed.

2. The public key can't live in <name>.json. It's made at first boot, so every node would change a tracked file, each with a different key. Put it in state/<name>/node.json, and stream that half.

3. An app could activate itself. Today an app may write its own state folder (fileSystem.js:81-107). If that rule carries over, an app can set active to true in its own node.json, which defeats the user's allow. node.json has to be writable by the node only.

4. A fresh node would show nothing, since every app starts inactive, including the one you'd use to turn apps on. I'd make the coded intrinsic list always active (coreFiles.js:27).

5. running repeats what jobs already holds (jobs.js:52), so the two can disagree. I'd paint it from jobs and drop it here.

Still open: the mount block, the file name per side for desk and agent (ubi's point), the fields in use today, and identity's fifth field, "(public)", which has no name.

ubi: better. A key per node, made at first boot, answers my key question, and the state folder is now out of git. Four things left:

1. The private key can't be in node.json as written. You have that file's changes streamed out, face included. Give the private key its own file that is never streamed.

2. The new state folder would be readable. The read gate refuses state by the name relay-state (fileSystem.js:184, :209), so spirit/state/ passes it and the static route would serve the keys. The gate has to know the new name before the first key is written.

3. The public key is still listed in <name>.json. That file is in git and is the same on every node, so a per-node key belongs in node.json.

4. active and running don't cover everything yet. Who sets active on a fresh node, when nobody can log in until login is active? And one app can have several jobs (jobs.js:468), so a single running flag can't describe them.
wsl: correction: the unnamed "(public)" field is identity's fourth, not its fifth.

cw: better, yes. The box answers my Q1, so I closed it. Four new things:

- Private keys in the new state folder could be read. The read gate only refuses folders named relay-state, so any app could fetch that one. It must be shut before the first key is made.
- Only 7 of the 23 shell apps name a server. If the app server makes the key on first boot, the other 16 never get one. I would have the node make it when the app is activated.
- "active" set by the user means a fresh node shows nothing, not even login or files. I would keep intrinsic apps always active.
- "running" on disk stays true after a crash, and the job row already says it live. I would store "start at boot" instead, and read running from the job row.

On the key that wsl and ubi raised: my answer is my new Q2.
all, better?

cw: better on the key for shell-only apps. Three things in this version:

- Dropping the server name breaks 5 apps. Chatter's server has another name, chatClerver, and deskDetails, falloutHistory, ruleDetails and stackFrameCheckDetail all use the desk server. Today each says so in "server". Either a face may name its server, or those four move inside desk as its panels and chatter and its server take one name. I recommend moving them.
- A key made when the file is first served means a read writes state, and an inactive app gets a key from a mere fetch. I would have the node make every missing key at boot, for both kinds of app.
- "The spirit folder is the boundary to intrinsic" conflicts with all apps living in it. Non-intrinsic apps would sit inside that boundary. The boundary should stay the coded list.

Q2 still stands: this version keeps the public key in the tracked file.

wsl: better, and shell-only apps now get a key. Three points:

1. Making a key the first time a file is served turns a read into a write, even for an app nobody activated. I'd use cw's moment for every app: the node makes the key when the app is activated, and intrinsic apps get theirs at first boot.

2. "Including face" clashes with your G41.33 ruling that a face with no star keeps today's restrictions and today's stream (faceHome.js:401). I'd stream node.json to a starred face only.

3. One <name>.js can't be both sides. Desk and agent each have two different programs named that today, and one file would send the server's code to the browser. I'd name them <name>.js for the shell and <name>Server.js for the node.

The private key in node.json is still in this version, and ubi's and my fix stands: give it its own file, never streamed.

cw: better on the key for shell-only apps. Three things in this version:

- Dropping the server name breaks 5 apps. Chatter's server has another name, chatClerver, and deskDetails, falloutHistory, ruleDetails and stackFrameCheckDetail all use the desk server. Today each says so in "server". Either a face may name its server, or those four move inside desk as its panels and chatter and its server take one name. I recommend moving them.

- "The spirit folder is the boundary to intrinsic" conflicts with all apps living in it. Non-intrinsic apps would sit inside that boundary. The boundary should stay the coded list.

Q2 still stands: this version keeps the public key in the tracked file.

# all files here are INTRINSIC and belong to "core".

- some WILL read and write node-owned state in "run://spirit/state/"
- only the node writes it's state, the shell can only attempt to write state by using verbs.

# first we create the following folders

- run://spirit/app/
- run://spirit/state/ (.gitignored) 

# And we create the following files

- run://spirit/app/server/server.js
- run://spirit/app/server/server.json
- run://spirit/state/server/node.json

# we make the file run://spirit/app/server/server.js a hello-world shell app AND server app, that can persist one boolean value, in "run://spirit/state/server/data.json", { serving:true|false} with a UI that allows to toggle that bool on and off.

- node state WILL live in "run://spirit/state/data.json" (oos)

- apps in the new folder are mounted by the new core module "run://spirit/app/mount.js", which inserts app functionality in the javaScript object spirit.app, when it's "required"
|
- "run://spirit/app/mount.js" will scan "run://spirit/app/" for servers or shell components on behalf of either, node or shell.

- "run://spirit/app/appSelector/rowElement.js"

### for now, node will change the smallest possible bit

wsl: a good small proof: one app, both sides. Six things it has to settle:

1. The gates come first. Today any page can read spirit/state/ (fileSystem.js:193), and the server can't write data.json there, because spirit/ counts as core (:182) and own state only knows process/js (:86). I'd make the state folder unreadable except through the node, with one exception so the app can write its own data.json. node.json stays node-only.

2. The verbs need names. The toggle and spirit.app are new interface, so they need peer review and your yes. I'd name them in this box before any red.

ubi: a good first proof, small and all new. Checked against the tree at 9fa70a86. Six things:

1. State protection comes first. spirit/run/spirit/state/ isn't ignored by git today, and the read gate would serve it (fileSystem.js:209). Do both before the first file lands there.

2. The title needs a rule: which one wins when a name is in both places? I'd say the new one wins and the node says so at boot.

3. The node side is more than mount.js. Five places assume process/js or its state path: the boot scan (jobs.js:521, :569), the pipe path (appClient.js:80), grants (apiAuth.js:158) and the app's own state (fileSystem.js:85). mount.js should answer those too, or they keep missing the new folder.

4. The toggle needs a way to reach the server. If that's a new verb, the box should name it, for review and your yes. It should also say whether a face with no star may call it.

5. The scan needs a rule, because app/ also holds mount.js and appSelector/. I'd count a folder as an app only if it has <name>/<name>.json, so appSelector/ isn't read as one.

6. One server.js on both sides conflicts with wsl's point on goal/G43: the page gets the server's code. Harmless for hello-world, but it would set the pattern for desk. I'd prove the two-file shape here.
wsl: correction: the core-file refusal is at fileSystem.js:186, not :182. The own-state pattern is at :85.

cw: right size for a first proof, and spirit.app is free: nothing uses it today. Five things, from the tree at 9fa70a86:

- There are two shells, and each finds apps its own way. Desk runs on the old one, which you kept for your own careful steps. I recommend the new shell only. That is my Q1.
- The node half is the real work. Only the old process folder may start a server, own state or get a pipe, and four core modules each check that path: jobs, fileSystem, appClient and appServer. All of it needs your grant.

wsl: better. Sharing pipe, run and plugin keeps the node change small, and the <name>/<name>.json pattern means mount.js, run.js and appSelector/ aren't taken for apps. spirit.app and spirit.state are both free. Three notes:

1. run.js must not read the description. Today's start code checks kind and operated (jobs.js:524), which your new shape doesn't have. It should take a script, state folder, pipe and args, with old and new each supplying them.
